WMatrix¶

This class is the one that is mainly interacted with, and handles periodically driven transition matrices. The periodic driving is modeled through a driving symbol, which must be provided at initialisation. If this is not provided, an attempt is made to infer this from the input. The class provides methods for calculating transition matrices at equilibrium, first-order driving matrices, computing conductivity coefficients, and evaluating frequency-dependent conductivities.

class stoch_imp.WMatrix.WMatrix(*args, ds=None, eq=0, **kwargs)[source]¶

Class handling driven transition matrices.

Variables:

  • mat – Internal sympy.Matrix representation of the transition matrix.

  • dim – Dimension of the system.

  • iter – Iterator over matrix indices.

  • ds – Symbol representing the driving parameter.

  • eq – Value at which to evaluate equilibrium (default is 0).

  • weq – Cached equilibrium matrix (EqMatrix), or None if not yet computed.

  • w1 – First-order derivative matrix (ConstantMatrix), or None if not yet computed.

  • coeff – Coefficient array for conductivity calculations, or None if not yet computed.

  • tol – Numerical tolerance used for validations.

  • is_symbolic – Boolean indicating whether the matrix is in symbolic form.

  • zero_index – Boolean indicating whether 0-based indexing is used.

Parameters:

  • ds (Symbol | None)

  • eq (float)

add_trans(i, j, r=1.0, ri=None, symm=True, simp=True)¶

Add a transition i –> j with rate r, and optionally symmetric transition j –> i with rate ri.

Parameters:

  • i (int) – Start index

  • j (int) – Target index

  • r (float | Expr) – Transition rate from i to j

  • ri (float | Expr | None) – Optional inverse rate (j to i)

  • symm (bool) – If True, adds j –> i with rate 1/r or ri

  • simp (bool) – If True, simplifies r and ri

Return type:

None
